text:
A frictional clutch-box, thrown in and out of gear by the lever at the bottom. This is used for connecting and disconnecting heavy machinery. The eye of the disk to the right has a slot which slides upon a long key or feather fixed on the shaft.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 47
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 47; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_047.html.

text:
Clutch-box. The pinion at the top gives a continuous rotary motion to the gear below, to which is attached half the clutch, and both turn loosely on the shaft. When it is desired to give motion to the shaft, the other part of the clutch, which slides upon a key or feather fixed in the shaft, is thrust into gear by the lever.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 48
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 48; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_048.html.

text:
The vertical shaft is made to drive the horizontal one in either direction, as may be desired, by means of the double-clutch and bevel-gears. The gears on the horizontal shaft are loose, and are driven in opposite directions by the third gear; the double-clutch slides upon a key or feather fixed on the horizontal shaft, which is made to rotate either to the right or left, according to the side on which it is engaged.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 53
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 53; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_053.html.

text:
Bayonet joint. On turning the part, A, it is released from the L-shaped slot in the socket, B, when it can be withdrawn.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 245
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 245; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_245.html.

text:
Another simple form of clutch for pulleys, consisting of a pin on the lower shaft and a pin on side of pulley. The pulley is moved lengthwise of the shaft by means of a lever or other means to bring its pin into or out of contact with the pin on shaft.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 361
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 361; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_361.html.

text:
A method of repairing chains, or tightening chains used as guys or braces. Link is made in two parts, one end of each is provided with swivel-nut, and other end with screw; the screw of each part fits into nut of other.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 399
